title: Finite-momentum pairing and magnetic halos in a spin-imbalanced Holstein model
authors: Chunhan Feng, George Batrouni, Richard Scalettar
abstract: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity, Cooper pairing at finite-momentum driven by spin imbalance, remains difficult to study numerically in two dimensions. The fermion sign problem in the spin-imbalanced attractive Hubbard model severely limits quantum Monte Carlo access to the low temperatures where pairing correlations are most pronounced. We show that the Holstein model, in which the effective attraction is retarded by phonon dynamics, strongly suppresses sign fluctuations under spin imbalance, enabling unbiased determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations deep in this regime. With increasing magnetization, zero-momentum pairing evolves into finite-momentum FFLO pairing, evidenced by oscillating real-space pair correlations and a shift of the pairing susceptibility peak to finite $\vec{Q}$. The finite-momentum susceptibility substantially exceeds its zero-momentum value. At high density $n \sim 0.875$, near magnetization $m \approx 1-n$ where the majority-spin density approaches half filling, FFLO pairing coexists with checkerboard charge-density-wave order at short range, while staggered longitudinal spin correlations emerge as a magnetic halo at larger distances. These spatial textures provide experimentally accessible signatures of finite-momentum pairing and motivate cold-atom realizations of FFLO physics.
summary: This work investigates finite-momentum pairing (FFLO superconductivity) in a spin-imbalanced system using the Holstein model. By employing DQMC, the authors overcome sign problem limitations to show that increasing spin imbalance drives the pairing into a finite-momentum state. The study reveals a rich interplay where FFLO pairing coexists spatially with charge-density-wave order and magnetic halo structures.
main_problem: The study of Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity, which involves Cooper pairing at finite momentum driven by spin imbalance, is challenging due to the fermion sign problem.
main_result:
The Holstein model allows for unbiased simulation of FFLO pairing, showing that increasing spin imbalance shifts pairing from zero to finite momentum ($\vec{Q} 
eq 0$) and coexisting with charge-density-wave order and magnetic halos.
method: Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations were employed to study the system's ground state properties.
model_or_system: The research uses the spin-imbalanced two-dimensional Holstein model, which incorporates phonon-mediated attraction, allowing it to bypass the severe sign fluctuations encountered in the attractive Hubbard model.
key_observables: Pairing susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{pair}}(\vec{Q})$), real-space pair correlations ($C_p(\vec{r})$), charge-density-wave order ($S_n(\vec{Q})$), and staggered longitudinal spin correlations ($C_z(\vec{r})$).
important_parameters: High density ($n \approx 0.875$) and varying magnetization ($m$), particularly near the regime $m \approx 1-n$.
main_assumptions: The Holstein model is used as an effective description, and the DQMC method is assumed to provide accurate results despite the complexity of the correlated state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shift of the pairing susceptibility peak to finite $\vec{Q}$ with increasing magnetization, and show spatial patterns of coexisting pairing, CDW, and magnetic halo correlations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the feasibility of simulating FFLO physics using the Holstein model, then quantifying the shift in pairing momentum, and finally detailing the complex spatial coexistence of pairing, CDW, and magnetic halo textures at high density.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between the Holstein model, FFLO physics, and the potential for realization in cold-atom platforms (like Rydberg atoms) makes this highly relevant to AMO physics.

FIG. 5. Pair susceptibility and charge and spin-Z structure factors. As functions of temperature T for two magnetizations, m ≈0.13 and 0.25. The dashed line marks the temperature T ∗below which the finite-momentum pair susceptibility exceeds its zero-momentum value, indicating the onset of FFLO pairing. At m ≈0.13, where the FFLO with a magnetic halo is observed, both Sn and Sz exhibit a sharp increase just below T ∗. In contrast, at m = 0.25, where no FFLO halo is observed, both structure factors remain sub- stantially smaller and show no comparable increase.
